paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery entry point; tested at desktop, mobile, preference emulations, no-JS, performance, privacy, accessibility, and repeated-scroll conditions.
Representative editorial article template and core reading journey.
Representative sport section/listing template; stands in for other editorial section pages.
Representative live/results data surface and interactive information template.
Representative HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture; the preference probe reports color-scheme: normal and black text while prefers-color-scheme: dark matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces and controls with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The consent overlay animation ignores reduced motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe still reports the 500 ms slideUp animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or reduce the slideUp transition inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: No explicit contrast or forced-colors adaptation is present.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast probe matches but color-scheme remains normal and scrollbarColor remains auto; the consent wall retains low-emphasis gray copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Test forced-colors and prefers-contrast, preserve control boundaries, and adapt scrollbar and muted-text colors.

findings.summary: Navigation state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS/DOM inspection found no view-transition declarations on this multi-page navigation surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for compatible same-origin article and section navigation, with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The long scrolling news surface does not use declarative scroll-state affordances.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no animation-timeline scroll()/view() usage on the 15,984 px homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-driven animations only where scroll-linked feedback adds value, and respect reduced motion.

findings.summary: Carousel and horizontal navigation affordances use small tab controls without platform-native gesture evidence.
findings.evidence: axe reports seven nested interactive carousel tab patterns; CSS inspection did not expose scroll-snap/overscroll treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Build carousels around scroll-snap and non-nested controls, retaining keyboard and touch semantics.

findings.summary: The very long homepage has no visible scroll progress or scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is 15,984 px tall while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container-type: scroll-state for useful sticky-header or progress feedback.

findings.summary: Dropdown navigation lacks modern anchored positioning evidence.
findings.evidence: The page exposes several dropdown navigation controls, but inspected CSS contains no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for dropdowns and tooltips.

findings.summary: A full-page consent wall obscures all editorial content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show a dimmed page with the consent panel occupying most of the viewport before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a compact, non-blocking consent experience and defer non-essential tracking until a clear choice.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is an ad-hoc div rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM probe reports zero dialog, popover, or details elements and one custom overlay; axe reports its scrollable text is not keyboard accessible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a modal <dialog> with correct focus management and accessible overflow, or a non-modal banner if blocking is unnecessary.

findings.summary: Consent and layered navigation dominate the first viewport over the news content.
findings.evidence: The screenshots show utility ticker, masthead, category bar, team-logo strip, dimmer, and consent panel before usable content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce stacked chrome and make the first viewport content-led after a compact privacy choice.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows horizontally at 360 px.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive reports scrollWidth 618 px versus visual viewport 360 px, an overflow of 258 px; the article template itself reflows correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 618 px minimum/fixed-width constraint and contain horizontally scrolling navigation locally.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-centric rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: Inspected accessible CSS contains media queries but no @container rules, while cards and navigation are reused across widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable cards, scoreboards, and navigation modules.

findings.summary: Several controls are undersized or lack a visible authored focus indicator.
findings.evidence: Focus probe found 30x30 team links and an edition button with outline none; many ticker links are only 11 px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 touch hit areas where practical and a clear :focus-visible treatment on every control.

findings.summary: Reading any story requires resolving a coercive full-screen consent/subscription gate first.
findings.evidence: Fresh-session screenshots show no path to continue reading without accepting tracking or choosing the paid rejection route.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow core news reading with a clear reject-non-essential option that does not require subscription.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 9.95 s, FCP 5.96 s, CLS 0.105, and a performance score of 0.48.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce critical JavaScript, reserve layout space, and defer below-fold/third-party work.

findings.summary: Layout stability misses the good CLS threshold in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports CLS 0.105; the image audit also finds 26 images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio to images and reserve space for banners, embeds, and ads.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Trace recorded four long tasks, an 846.56 ms longest task, and 837.66 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, defer non-critical scripts, and schedule background work at lower priority.

findings.summary: The homepage ships an expensive critical network load.
findings.evidence: HAR records 185 requests and 4.38 MB transferred, including 57 scripts totaling 2.75 MB and 16 fonts totaling 510 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical chains, consolidate fonts, prioritize the LCP resource, and defer non-essential scripts.

findings.summary: Large script and third-party payloads dominate the load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags about 1.25 MB unused JavaScript; HAR attributes 3.81 MB and 171 requests to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tags and unused bundles, load analytics conditionally, and gate advertising code until needed/consented.

findings.summary: Interactive semantics contain serious accessibility errors.
findings.evidence: axe finds an unnamed link, seven nested interactive controls, and invalid list children.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every link an accessible name, avoid nested focusable descendants, and restore valid list/control semantics.

findings.summary: Landmark and focus structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: axe finds nested/duplicate complementary landmarks, 11 regions outside landmarks, and a consent text scroller without keyboard access.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one labelled landmark per purpose, contain content in landmarks, and make every scrollable region keyboard reachable.

findings.summary: The homepage reflows poorly and exposes undersized targets.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the homepage overflows by 258 px; focus probe finds 30x30 team links and 11 px-high ticker links.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix mobile reflow, enlarge hit areas, keep user scaling enabled, and provide equivalents for embedded media.

findings.summary: The homepage emits repeated console and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured seven errors, including Amazon ad API misuse, missing euconsent-v2, localhost connection refusal, and SSL failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct ad/consent initialization and remove or repair failing telemetry endpoints.

findings.summary: Image assets are not consistently sound or efficient.
findings.evidence: The image audit finds 26 missing dimensions, 55 missing srcset, 98 legacy-format images, and three missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height and srcset/sizes, use modern image formats, and repair missing alternatives.

findings.summary: Some important links are not crawlable URLs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse crawlable-anchors audit fails on consent and login links using javascript:void(0); the login link in recon resolves to a fragment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and buttons for actions.

findings.summary: No sitemap is advertised at the conventional location or in robots.txt.
findings.evidence: robots.txt is reachable and permits core content, but /sitemap.xml returns 404 and no Sitemap directive was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish and advertise an XML sitemap covering canonical article and section URLs.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but critical headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Header audit finds no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff; cookie audit reports 33 of 33 observed cookies as insecure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Secure, HttpOnly where applicable, and explicit SameSite policies.

findings.summary: The default page load has a very large tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit sees 44 third-party origins and eight known trackers; HAR attributes 171 requests and 3.81 MB to non-main origins before a consent decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential tracking until consent, minimize vendors/events, and batch necessary analytics.

findings.summary: The visible sign-in entry does not expose a modern authentication path.
findings.evidence: Recon finds “Iniciar sesión” as a fragment link and the loaded public surface contains no WebAuthn/passkey capability marker; no permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a real sign-in route and offer passkey authentication; keep permission requests tied to user gestures.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete and referrer leakage is permissive.
findings.evidence: Headers omit CSP, HSTS, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff; Referrer-Policy is unsafe-url, although X-Frame-Options is SAMEORIGIN.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP/frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and nosniff.

findings.summary: Component language tags include invalid locale syntax.
findings.evidence: axe reports two scoreboard components using invalid lang="esES" despite the document correctly using lang="es".
findings.suggestedFix: Use valid BCP 47 tags such as es-ES and verify bidi/logical layout behavior.

findings.summary: Article date formatting is hard-coded to one Spanish presentation despite locale variants.
findings.evidence: The article renders “22/07/2026 - 05:44 CEST” while homepage metadata advertises es, es-MX, es-US, and en variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Render dates, numbers, and scores with Intl for the active locale.

findings.summary: Consent uses a paid-rejection dark pattern.
findings.evidence: The only prominent choices are “Acepto y continúo gratis” and “Rechazo y me suscribo”, framing tracking acceptance as free and rejection as paid.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally prominent accept and reject-non-essential choices without financial penalty or confirmshaming.

findings.summary: Privacy consent is coupled to subscription purchase.
findings.evidence: The full-screen gate directs users who reject cookie installation into a subscription path rather than a proportionate privacy choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Decouple privacy refusal from subscription and disclose any paid offer separately with clear terms and cancellation.

findings.summary: Most homepage images use legacy formats and lack responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, the audit reports 98 legacy formats, zero modern formats, 55 without srcset, and 22 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP candidates with srcset/sizes, retain fallbacks, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Substantial background/third-party work is loaded before it provides reader value.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 171 third-party requests and 2.75 MB of scripts; the trace records 838 ms blocking time while a consent wall prevents reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer, conditionally load, or remove advertising/analytics work until consent and proximity to use.

findings.summary: Third-party resource cost is disproportionate for a text-led news entry page.
findings.evidence: Non-main origins account for 3.81 MB of 4.38 MB transferred, with 44 third-party origins and eight known trackers.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove redundant vendors, self-host essential assets, and load embeds on demand.

findings.summary: Repeated full-page scrolling produces large retained heap growth.
findings.evidence: After ten top-to-bottom scroll cycles, the heap summary grows from 999,223 to 1,486,097 nodes and from 56.8 MB to 79.0 MB self size. Dynamic feed loading may explain part of the growth, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile repeated scrolling with baseline/target/final snapshots and release feed nodes, observers, and vendor allocations that no longer serve visible content.

findings.summary: The initial page memory footprint is unusually large for a news listing.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap contains 999,223 nodes and 56.8 MB total self size before exercising the long feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce DOM depth/card retention and defer third-party widgets and below-fold modules.

taskList.title: Remove the coercive full-screen consent/subscription wall and block trackers until a fair choice
Reduce third-party JavaScript, long tasks, and critical transfer cost
Fix mobile homepage overflow, hit areas, and focus visibility
Deploy complete security headers and secure cookie attributes
Repair overlay, link, control, and landmark semantics
Modernize responsive image delivery and reserve image space
Add dark, reduced-motion, and high-contrast adaptations
Profile and bound heap growth during repeated feed scrolling
